The DCE iron ore futures continued to decline today, with the benchmark I2609 contract finally closingat 747.5 yuan/ton, down 2.61% from the previous session and extending losses markedly. Portside spot prices also fell in tandem, dropping 10-15 yuan/ton from a day earlier. Traders showed diverging approaches-some refrained from quoting and stood on the sidelines, while others offered cargoes in line with market conditions; steel mills remained cautious, with strong intentions to push prices down and a slower procurement pace, dampening overall market sentiment. Trading was subdued, and spot transaction volumes remained limited as of now. According to SMM survey data released on June 17, the blast furnace operating rate among 242 sampled steel mills stood at 90.67%, up 0.20 percentage point week-on-week, while the average daily hot metal output of the sample mills reached 2.465 million tons, an increase of 5,300 tons from the prior week. However, looking ahead to next week, as steel mills face growing margin pressure, maintenance plans are increasing, which may mark a near-term turning point for hot metal production. Demand is expected to weaken marginally, while persistent supply-side pressure and the off-season effect in the industry jointly weigh on iron ore prices, exacerbating the decline. In the short term, pessimistic sentiment dominates the market, and DCE iron ore prices are likely to continue their bottoming-out process. Linked asset: 17062026chines324.jpg
Source: Metals Market Index (MMI)

The iron ore benchmark contract I2609 traded on a weak note today, finally closing at 747 yuan/ton,down 1.13%. Port spot prices remained broadly unchanged from yesterday. Traders showed moderate willingness to sell, while steel mills stayed cautious and purchased only on an as-needed basis, with weak restocking appetite. Overall market sentiment was subdued, and trading activity was thin, with light turnover. With the holiday approaching, market trading has turned quieter, and both spot and futures prices have fluctuated within a narrow range. Looking ahead to next week, as hot metal output is expected to peak and then decline, demand for iron ore is likely to weaken. Meanwhile, falling ocean freight rates have undermined cost support. In the near term, iron ore prices are expected to continue to fluctuate with a weak bias.

The DCE iron ore futures continued to hit boƩom today, with the most-traded I2609 contract closing at 739.5 yuan/mt,down 0.87%. Port spot prices fell by 3-5 yuan/mt from pre-holiday levels. Traders showed low selling enthusiasm, with many holding off from offering. Wait-and-see sentiment intensified among steel mills, and only a few purchased as needed. The overall trading atmosphere was sluggish. As of now, very few deals were concluded. Last week, SMM total global iron ore shipments reached 32.98 million mt, down 7.62% WoW, while cumulative shipments were up 1.9% YoY. Shipments from both Australia and Brazil declined, while those from non-mainstream countries edged up. In addition, SMM total China iron ore arrivals stood at 27.81 million mt last week, down 7.14% WoW, with cumulative growth of 5.85% YoY. This week, supply pressure eased slightly. However, as steel mill losses deepened and blast furnace maintenance increased, hot metal output is expected to decline this week. Iron ore demand weakened, leaving ore prices under downward pressure.

Today, DCE iron ore futures opened weak in the morning session and saw a modest recovery in the afternoon,with the most-traded I2609 contract closing at 738.5 yuan/mt, down 0.54% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices held steady from the previous day. Traders mostly followed market trends, with moderate quoting enthusiasm. Steel mills made fewer inquiries, and spot trading volume was moderate as of the time of writing. This week, the SMM survey showed the impact from blast furnace maintenance was 1.1633 million mt, up 31,600 mt WoW. Iron ore demand weakened, and hot metal may pull back due to maintenance and environmental protection-driven production restrictions. In addition, expectations for the ninth round of coke price increases fermented. Weak sentiment in coal and coke spilled over to iron ore, coupled with falling oil prices and interest rate hike expectations weighing on overall sentiment in the ferrous metals market. Iron ore prices are expected to remain in the doldrums in the short term.

Today, DCE iron ore futures strengthened in the morning session and dipped slightly in the afternoon today,with the most-traded I2609 contract closing at 744 yuan/mt, up 0.74% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices rose 4-9 yuan/mt from the prior day. Miner activity was moderate, with steel mills primarily purchasing for essential restocking; spot trading volume has been mediocre thus far. On the fundamentals front, according to an SMM survey, the daily average hot metal output of sampled steel mills this week was 2.4607 million mt, down 4,300 mt WoW. Pig iron production has reached an inflection point, and iron ore demand is expected to weaken going forward. On the news front, market rumors of tightening iron ore supply disrupted the near-term bearish sentiment. Taking all factors into account, iron ore prices are likely to move sideways in the short term, while the medium and long-term outlook remains bearish.

text:
Today, DCE iron ore futures weakened, with the most-traded contract I2609 closing at 735 yuan/mt,down 1.08% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices fell 5-7 yuan/mt from the previous day. Traders showed modest willingness to quote, while steel mills had a strong desire to push for lower prices. As of now, spot trading volume was relatively low. Looking ahead, amid the steel off-season, export demand for finished steel continued to weaken, driving pig iron production to a turning point, and iron ore demand is expected to shrink further. Additionally, rumors of environmental protection-driven production restrictions, combined with weakening downstream export data, triggered market pessimism, leaving ore prices more likely to fall than rise. In the short term, iron ore prices may trend sideways in a tug-of-war between longs and shorts, while the medium- and long-term outlook is persistently bearish.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended strong today, pulling back slightly near the close. The most-traded I2609contract closed at 748 yuan/ mt, up 0.81% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices rose 8-11 yuan/mt from the prior day. Trader quoting activity was moderate, steel mills maintained a strong wait-and-see stance, and spot trading volumes were moderate as of now. Looking ahead, iron ore port data for this period, according to an SMM survey, showed a slight destocking. Total inventory reached 148.66 million mt, down 690,000 mt MoM, while port pick-up volume edged down 38,000 mt to 3.23 million mt. The destocking was mainly driven by a decline in port arrivals. Overall, the iron ore supply side remained loose. On the news front, market rumors were frequent, and the tug-of-war between longs and shorts was fierce, with no clear divergence yet. With fundamentals and sentiment intertwined, ore prices are likely to continue moving sideways in the short term.

text:
Today on the DCE iron ore futures first weakened and then strengthened, with contract I2609 finally closing at 746 yuan/ton,up 0.67% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices were unchanged from the previous trading day. Trader activity was moderate, and steel mills purchased on an as-needed basis, with spot transaction volumes remaining lackluster so far. In the short term, iron ore supply continues to ease. According to SMM statistics, China's iron ore arrivals reached 29.33 million tonnes last week, up 5.47% month-on-month and 5.94% year-on-year. Meanwhile, the latest SMM data shows that total inventory across 35 ports stood at approximately 148 million tonnes, with destocking beginning to slow down. As downstream demand softens, mounting supply-side pressure on iron ore continues to cap upside price potential. At the same time, a mix of bullish and bearish rumours on the news front may drive modest upward price probes in the near term. Taken together, the market is likely to maintain a range-bound oscillatory pattern over the short term.

Today, the iron ore market on the Dalian Commodity Exchange showed a volatile trading pattern,with contract I2609 eventually closing at 747 yuan/ton, up +0.61% compared with the previous trading session. Port spot prices rose by 0-3 yuan/ton from the previous day. Trader activity was moderate, while steel mill purchases remained largely needôbased; as of now, spot market transaction volumes have been average. The current iron ore fundamentals continue to show a bearish bias. Supply remains loose, with no clear sign of reversal, while demand has entered a plateau and is expected to continue its downward trend in the future. This week's SMM survey data indicate that blast furnace maintenance resulted in hot metal output impact of 1,156,300 tonnes, down by 48,700 tonnes weekôonôweek, with the projected impact for next week reaching 1,200,500 tonnes. On the news front, most factors are marginal disturbances, with bullish news taking the lead but not yet pointing to a directional trend. Therefore, considering all factors, shortôterm iron ore prices are expected to maintain a rangeôbound consolidation pattern. Linked asset: 30062026chinesew.jpg
Source: Metals Market Index (MMI)

text:
The Dalian Commodity Exchange iron ore market showed volatile trading today, with contract I2609 finally closing at 733 yuan/ton,down 1.68% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices fell by 10-12 yuan/ton from the prior day. Trader activity was moderate, while steel mill inquiries increased; however, spot transaction volumes remained generally modest as of now. Iron ore demand is expected to continue declining in July. On the one hand, steel is affected by the off-season weather, with both domestic demand and exports declining, putting downward pressure on prices. At the same time, the ninth round of coke price hikes has been implemented, and expectations for a tenth round remain strong, further compressing steel mill profits and thus heightening expectations of production cuts. According to this week's SMM survey, sample steel mill output stood at 2.456 million tons, down 4,700 tons from the previous week, and some mills have already begun scheduling maintenance plans, suggesting that hot metal output will likely decline further. In summary, the short-term outlook for iron ore prices is bearish.

Today's DCE iron ore futures showed weakness after rallying in the night session.Contract I2609 settled at 740 yuan/ton, up 0.48% from the previous trading day. Port spot prices rose 5-8 yuan/ton versus the prior session. Trader activity was moderate, with steel mills procuring on an as-needed basis; spot trading volumes have remained unremarkable so far.
The iron ore supply-demand fundamentals remain largely stable, with supply on the loose side. Going forward, the pace of mine shipments is expected to slow, keeping the overall picture relatively steady. On the demand side, Southeast Asian steel exports have entered the oﬀ-season, prompting regional traders to actively cut prices to compete for market share. As a result, domestic export demand has begun to soften. However, domestic steel inventories still have buﬀer room, and this is unlikely to trigger production-cut intentions among steel mills in the near term. On the news front, aside from supply-tightening rumors for speciﬁc varieties, there are no events decisive enough to drive market direction.
Taken together, iron ore prices are expected to trade in a range-bound pattern in the short term.

Today, iron ore futures on the DCE traded weaker, with contract 12609 finally closing at 734 yuan/ton,down 1.74% from the previous trading day. Port spot prices fell by 3-8 yuan/ton from the prior day. Trader activity was moderate, while steel mill purchases were mainly for replenishment; spot market transaction volumes have been average so far.
According to SMM surveys, iron ore inventory at 35 major ports nationwide this week stood at 148.30 million tons, down 36,000 tons week-on-week, indicating a slight overall destocking. Meanwhile, average daily outbound shipments from ports rose by 68,000 tons to 3.298 million tons, reflecting relatively sound short-term demand. Next week, arriving shipments are expected to increase further, tilting resource supply toward looser conditions; on the demand side, as hot metal output gradually declines, outbound shipment volumes are likely to follow suit. Support for iron ore prices is weakening, but n the near term, prices are likely to fluctuate within a range, as supply and demand dynamics remain largely in line with market expectations.

Today, DCE iron ore futures trended strong but pulled back slightly in the afternoon.Contract 12609 closed at 738 yuan/mt, up 0.14% from the previous trading day. Port spot prices rose 2-3 yuan/mt from the previous day. Traders were active in quoting, steel mills purchased as needed, inquiry interest was moderate, with spot transaction volumes remaining low
Looking ahead, as the downstream enters the off-season and the pace of mine shipments slows, the supply side of iron ore is expected to tighten slightly, though the overall loose pattern will be hard to change. Last week, SMM's global iron ore shipments totaled 35.16 million mt, up 1.53% WoW, with cumulative YoY growth of 1.77%. Among them, Australia's shipments edged down 6% WoW, while Brazil's surged nearly 20% WoW, and non-mainstream countries' shipments edged up slightly WoW. Among the four major miners, shipments from Rio Tinto and FMG declined. In addition, last week, SMM's China iron ore arrivals totaled 28.78 million mt, edging down 1.88% WoW, with cumulative YoY growth of 6.07%. Overall, iron ore prices are likely to fluctuate within a range in the short term, while the long-term outlook remains bearish.

text:
Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended weaker today, with contract 12609 closing at 735.5 yuan/mt,down 0.47% from the previous trading day. Port spot prices fell about 1-2 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Traders were moderately active in offering, and steel mills mostly restocked as needed.
As of now, spot transaction volumes were moderate.
Iron ore demand is expected to continue declining this week. According to SMM statistics, the hot metal impact from blast furnace maintenance between July 4 and July 10 was 1.2637 million mt, up 77,800 mt WoW, and the impact is expected to increase by another 64,500 mt next week to 1.3282 million mt. In the short term, iron ore demand is expected to keep contracting, price support will gradually weaken, and overall ore prices may fluctuate within a range in a bearish trend. Today, DCE iron ore futures trended weakly, with contract 12609 closing at 746 yuan/mt, up 0.88% from the previous trading day.Port spot prices rose by about 5-7 yuan/mt from the previous day. Trader activity was average, and steel mills purchased on an as-needed basis. As of now, spot trading sentiment been
The latest SMM survey data further confirmed the weakening trend in iron ore demand. Statistics show that the national blast furnace operating rate fell to 89.78%, and daily average pig iron production dropped to 2.4406 million mt, down 15,400 mt MoM. Additionally, affected by commemorative events in Tangshan, local environmental protection-related maintenance is expected to intensify, and the weakening trend in hot metal output is likely to strengthen further. In the short term, the bearish fundamental backdrop has deepened. However, given the currently high proportion of short positions in the futures market, selling pressure is nearly exhausted, and the downward momentum for prices has begun to fade. Short-term ore prices are likely to consolidate and move sideways. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether a reduction in short positions could drive a price rebound.

text:
Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended weak today, with contract 12609 closing at 745.5 yuan/mt, up 0.27% from the previous trading day.Port spot prices ranged from -2 to +3 yuan/mt compared with the previous trading day. Trader activity was moderate, steel mills made few inquiries, and of now, spot transaction volumes were low.
According to the SMM survey, total inventory at the 10 main ports stood at 108.14 million mt, down 1.32 million mt MoM. Among them, fines destocking slowed, lump ore destocking was good, and pellet inventory was at an extremely low level. In the short term, pellet and lump premiums are expected to remain firm, while fines prices will find it difficult to break higher as inventory accumulates. Demand side, steel mills' purchase willingness showed a weakening trend MoM. In the short term, iron ore prices are expected to continue fluctuating with limited upside and resistance to downward pressure on prices.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended weaker today, with contract 12609 closing at 751.5 yuan/mt, up 0.87% from the previous trading day.Port spot prices rose 2-5 yuan/mt from the prior trading day. Trader activity was moderate, and steel mills mainly purchased for essential restocking. As of now spot trading volumes were moderate.
SMM's latest statistics showed that total iron ore inventory at 35 main ports nationwide was 147.16 million mt, down 1.14 million mt WoW. Over the same period, the daily average port pick-up volume edged down by 23,000 mt to 3.275 million mt. This week, affected by typhoons and persistent rainy weather, port operations were disrupted, vessel berthing and unloading efficiency dropped significantly, and port congestion intensified. On the demand side, as hot metal production of steel mill blast fumaces continued to decline, the daily average port pick-up volume pulled back slightly. With increasing blast furnace maintenance at steel mills, hot metal production is still expected to decline further. Therefore, from a fundamental perspective, short-term support for iron ore prices is expected to continue weakening.

text:
Today, iron ore prices on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) came under pressure, with the main contract I2609 finally settling at 744.5 yuan/ton,down approximately 0.47% from the previous session. Port spot prices fell by about 4-6 yuan/ton from the previous trading day. Traders' quotation enthusiasm weakened, and steel mills' purchases were mostly for replenishment needs. As of now, spot transaction volumes have been relatively low. As of last Friday, global iron ore total shipments reached 30.381 million tons, a decrease of 14% month-on-month. Among them, shipments from both Australia and Brazil saw significant reductions. During the same period, iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports were 25.015 million tons, down 13% month-on-month. The supply side of iron ore has tightened in the short term, but given the high port inventory level (147 million tons), the overall supply side remains relatively loose. As pig iron production enters a downward trend, iron ore demand is expected to weaken further. Therefore, from a fundamental perspective, iron ore prices are likely to fluctuate within a narrow range this week, with a tendency to decline.

Today, the iron ore market showed relatively strong performance on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE), with the benchmark contractI2609 finally closing at 760.5 yuan/ton, up 1.81%. Qingdao port spot prices remained firm, rising by approximately 10-12 yuan/ton from the previous trading day. Traders became more active, while steel mills, apart from rigid replenishment, showed generally low purchasing willingness. Spot transaction volumes have remained modest so far. In terms of mill maintenance schedules, iron ore demand is expected to decline further. According to SMM statistics, the blast furnace maintenance-induced hot metal impact for this week (July 11-July 17) is 1.3434 million tons, an increase of 70,100 tons from the previous week. For next week (July 18-July 24), the impact is projected to reach 1.4109 million tons, up by 67,500 tons week-on-week. On the news front, the strike at Port Hedland and the upcoming shipping restrictions are likely to tighten supply side in the short term. Taken together, iron ore prices may see a modest bottom rebound in the near term, but are still expected to remain within a range-bound fluctuation pattern overall.

Today, the iron ore market showed strong performance on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE), with the benchmark contract I2609ultimately closing at 762 RMB/ton, up 1.13%. At Qingdao port, spot prices edged up by about 0-2 RMB/ton from the previous trading day, as trading volumes remained thin. Traders' offer enthusiasm was generally moderate, while steel mills showed weak purchasing interest. Spot transactions so far today have been limited. SMM survey data confirm continued weakness in iron ore demand. According to the survey results, the blast furnace operating rate across 242 Chinese steel mills this week stood at 89.79%, and the average daily hot metal output of sampled mills reached 2.4382 million tons, down 2,400 tons from the previous week. The fundamental support for iron ore prices continues to weaken. On the news front, some mining firms are reportedly set to implement vessel loading restrictions at ports as early as tomorrow, sparking intense market sentiment that drove up futures prices. However, such factors are unlikely to provide sustained support for iron ore prices over the longer term. Considering supply-demand dynamics and sentiment, iron ore prices are likely to remain firm in the short term until sentiment fades and prices revert to fundamental drivers.

text:
The iron ore market saw narrow fluctuations today, with the DCE main contract I2609 eventually closing at 759.5 RMB/ton,unchanged from the previous day. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell by 2-5 RMB/ton compared to the previous trading day. Traders sold goods in line with market conditions, while steel mills showed improved purchasing willingness, and market trading activity was better than yesterday. Among them, the transaction price for PB fines at Rizhao Port was 708 RMB/ton. According to SMM survey data, as of July 16, the total inventory across the 10 ports monitored by SMM stood at 106.27 million tonnes, down 1.87 million tonnes from the previous period. Inventories of fines, concentrates, and pellets declined, while lump ore saw a slight accumulation. This indicates that overall iron ore demand remains resilient. Although market chatter suggests that environmental protection production restrictions have begun in Tangshan, they have not yet affected hot metal output. The iron ore fundamentals remain relatively stable. However, given expectations of reduced supply of Ukrainian concentrates due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and with the upcoming July Politburo meeting fueling strong market expectations for policy support in the second half of the year, a short-term price rebound is anticipated.

The iron ore market traded sideways today, with the DCE main contract I2609 eventually closing at 762 RMB/ton, up 0.53% from the previous day'sclosing price. Spot prices mostly followed with gains of 0-2 RMB/ton. Traders sold goods in line with market conditions; as the weekend approached, steel mills showed weaker purchasing willingness, and market trading activity was generally moderate.As of July 17, the latest SMM statistics show that iron ore inventory across 35 major ports nationwide totaled 145.13 million tonnes, down 2.03 million tonnes from the previous period, marking another round of destocking. During the same period, the average daily port oŏake fell slightly by 55,000 tonnes to 3.22 million tonnes. This week, due to short-term weather disruptions, arrivals at some ports dropped notably, and resource replenishment tightened significantly. Looking ahead to next week, although iron ore demand is expected to weaken further, the US-Iran conflict and longterm contract negotiations will continue to create disturbances in the market. Prices are expected to maintain a range-bound fluctuation next week.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures moved sideways today, with the most-traded DCE I2609 contract closing at 758 yuan/mt, edging down 0.39%from yesterday's closing price. Spot prices fell by 0-5 yuan/mt in tandem; traders sold based on market conditions; steel mills purchased as needed, and overall market trading sentiment on Monday was subdued. Supply side, total global iron ore shipments tracked by SMM last week reached 30.98 million mt, up 2% WoW, with cumulative growth of 1% YoY. Shipments from Australia and Brazil both edged up, but those from non-mainstream countries dropped notably WoW, while the four major miners posted a slight increase. Meanwhile, total iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports last week came to 19.75 million mt, down 21% WoW but with cumulative growth of 4% YoY, mainly affected by typhoons and heavy rains; a recovery is expected this week. Demand side, steel mill shipments fell further due to the weather, weakening their willingness to purchase raw materials and in turn weighing on spot prices. Overall, ore prices are expected to continue their sideways consolidation in the short term

Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended weakly, with a slight recovery in the afternoon. The most-traded DCE I2609 contract closed at 749 yuan/mt,up 1.13%. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell about 5-12 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Trader quoting enthusiasm was mediocre, and steel mill purchase willingness was mediocre. As of now, spot cargo trading volumes were mediocre. Currently, supply-side pressure in iron ore has not yet become prominent, and overall inventory remains in a destocking trend. As of last weekend, total iron ore inventory across 35 main ports nationwide stood at 145.13 million mt, down 2.03 million mt WoW; daily average port pick-up volume edged down 55,000 mt to 3.22 million mt. Meanwhile, blast furnace maintenance intensity increased further. According to SMM statistics, the hot metal output impact from blast furnace maintenance this week was 1.3584 million mt, up 67,500 mt WoW. Next week, the hot metal impact is expected to be 1.5097 million mt, up 151,300 mt from this week, and the demand side is therefore expected to continue to decline. Looking at the overall supply-demand fundamentals, iron ore prices are expected to consolidate on a subdued note in the short term

Today, the DCE iron ore futures weakened today. The most-traded DCE i2609 contract closed at 739.5 yuan/mt, down 1.00%. The spot price at Qingdao Portfell around 4-8 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm in offering prices, while steel mills remained largely on the sidelines. As of now, spot trading volumes were moderate. According to this week's SMM survey, the capacity utilization rate of blast furnaces at sampled steel mills was 89.49%, down 0.50 percentage point WoW. Daily average hot metal production at sampled steel mills was 2.4247 million mt, down 13,500 mt WoW. Although this round of environmental protection-driven production restrictions was weaker than expected, hot metal production is expected to continue its downward trend. Meanwhile, environmental and safety inspection factors have not yet dissipated, and some steel mills may have temporary maintenance plans. Overall, blast furnace hot metal production is likely to keep declining in the short term, and iron ore demand is expected to remain weak. Therefore, iron ore prices are expected to consolidate with a bearish bias in the short term.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures moved strongly today. The most-traded DCE I2609 contract closed at 747.5 yuan/mt, up 0.74%. Spot prices at Qingdao Portrose roughly 5-8 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Trader activity was moderate, and inquiries from steel mills were limited. Spot trading was poor. Recently, steel mills' demand for iron ore has slowed. According to SMM data, inventories at the ten major ports totaled 105.63 million mt, down only 640,000 mt WoW. Based on current inventory structure, concentrate and lump ore destocking was relatively large, pellet inventories were at low levels, while fines saw a slight buildup. Demand side, off-season conditions persisted. Although environmental protection-driven production restrictions were relatively modest, the likelihood of steel mills voluntarily conducting blast furnace maintenance still exists. Next week's Politburo meeting expectations are heating up, potentially boosting market sentiment in the short term. On the whole, however, iron ore prices are expected to continue to move sideways in the near term.

text:
Today, the DCE iron ore futures futures consolidated on a subdued note. The most-traded DCE I2609 futures contract closed at 746 yuan/mt,down 0.13%. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell about 2-3 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Trader activity was moderate, with relatively few inquiries from steel mills. The current spot trading atmosphere is sluggish. From the current fundamentals, according to SMM statistics, total iron ore inventories at major ports nationwide were 144.92 million mt, down 210,000 mt MoM, with the overall inventory continuing to destock. Over the same period, the daily average port pick-up volume edged down 15,000 mt to 3.205 million mt. Despite a sharp decline in port arrivals, iron ore inventories still saw a slowdown in destocking, reflecting the current weak demand for iron ore. Looking ahead to next week, affected by a new round of environmental protection-driven production restrictions in Tangshan, the decline in hot metal output may widen, and iron ore prices will remain under pressure in the short term. Watch for any bullish policy signals from the Politburo meeting next week.

text:
Today, iron ore price fluctuations on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) were relatively narrow. The DCE benchmark contract I2609 closed at 741 yuan/ton,down 0.27%. Spot prices at Qingdao Port remained essentially flat compared with the previous trading day. Early morning saw active quotations from traders, while steel mills purchased on an as-needed basis, resulting in generally moderate spot trading activity. Recently, iron ore supply has shown an increase. According to SMM statistics, global iron ore shipments totalled 27.82 million tonnes, down 10% month-on-month but up 1% year-on-year on a cumulative basis. Shipments from Australia and Brazil both declined slightly; shipments from non-mainstream countries also decreased month- on-month, though those from India and Peru rebounded noticeably. Meanwhile, iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports totalled 30.32 million tonnes, surging 54% month-on-month and up 5% year-on-year cumulatively, with part of the increase driven by the discharge of vessels delayed by previous typhoons. On the demand side, blast furnace pig iron production continued its off-season downward trend, moving steadily lower. On the sentiment front, the US and Iran engaged in ceasefire negotiations, causing oil prices to fall, but the iron ore market showed little reaction. Overall, short-term iron ore prices are likely to remain in a range-bound pattern.

Today, iron ore prices experienced narrow fluctuations on the futures market. The DCE main contract I2609 closed at 741 yuan/ton, down0.20% from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port remained unchanged from the previous day. Traders showed generally average enthusiasm for quoting, while steel mills purchased on a need-to-use basis, resulting in moderate overall spot transaction activity. At present, the fundamentals of iron ore itself show little change, with demand entering a plateau phase. According to SMM statistics, the blast furnace maintenance this week has reduced hot metal output by 1.5678 million tons, an increase of 140,200 tons compared to last week's maintenance impact. Next week, the maintenance impact is expected to decrease by 207,500 tons week-on-week. On the supply side, as domestic mines gradually resume production, iron concentrate supply is expected to return to normal levels, and the concentrate premium may edge down slightly. In addition, the news front remains in a vacuum period, and the main contract is in its rollover phase, with no clear directional guidance for the near-term outlook. Market participants are closely watching the progress of negotiations and maintaining a strong wait-and-see attitude. Therefore, in the short term, iron ore prices are likely to continue their narrow range-bound oscillation.

Today, the iron ore market showed a weaker trend on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE). The main contract I2609 closed at 739 yuan/ton,down 0.27% from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell by 1-3 yuan/ton from the previous day. Traders showed moderate willingness to quote, while steel mills purchased mostly for essential needs, resulting in generally poor spot transaction seniment. In the short term, iron ore demand has edged down but is expected to pick up starting next week. According to SMM survey data, the blast furnace capacity utilization rate at sample steel mills stood at 88.90%, down 0.59 percentage point month-on-month, while average daily hot metal output fell by 16,000 tons to 2.4087 million tons. Next week, as environmental restrictions are lifted and most blast furnaces under maintenance resume production, hot metal output is likely to enter a growth phase. However, constrained by high iron ore inventories and lingering market uncertainties, prices are unlikely to break through upside resistance in the near term and may coninue to fluctuate within a narrow range.

text:
The iron ore market showed a lackluster performance on the spot today. The DCE main contract I2609 closed at 715 yuan/ton, down 3.31%from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell by 15-20 yuan/ton from the previous trading day. Traders showed relatively low willingness to quote, while steel mills' procurement was mostly for rigid demand, resulting in generally poor spot transaction sentiment. On the fundamental side, iron ore inventories continued to show structural divergence. The total inventory at 10 ports tracked by SMM stood at 106.92 million tons, up 1.29 million tons month-on-month, with stockpiles mainly accumulating in fines and lump ore, though pellet ore inventories remained at four-year lows. At the macro level, escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and their spillover effects triggered panic in the broader market, which transmitted to the iron ore futures market as a risk asset, leading to selling pressure and dragging overall prices lower. In the near term, iron ore prices are likely to continue declining amid panic sentiment.

The iron ore market showed a lackluster performance on the spot today. The DCE main contract I2609 closed at 715 yuan/ton, down3.31% from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell by 15-20 yuan/ton from the previous trading day. Traders showed relatively low willingness to quote, while steel mills' procurement was mostly for rigid demand, resulting in generally poor spot transaction sentiment. On the fundamental side, iron ore inventories continued to show structural divergence. The total inventory at 10 ports tracked by SMM stood at 106.92 million tons, up 1.29 million tons month-on-month, with stockpiles mainly accumulating in fines and lump ore, though pellet ore inventories remained at four-year lows. At the macro level, escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and their spillover effects triggered panic in the broader market, which transmiƩed to the iron ore futures market as a risk asset, leading to selling pressure and dragging overall prices lower. In the near term, iron ore prices are likely to continue declining amid panic sentiment.

Today's iron ore market performance on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) remained weak. The DCE benchmark contract I2609 closedat 698 yuan/ton, down 2.85% from the previous trading session. Qingdao port spot prices fell by 9-12 yuan/ton from the previous day. Traders showed low willingness to quote, while steel mills purchased only for rigid needs, resulting in sluggish overall spot transactions. At present, there is no change in the fundamentals of the iron ore market, and supply is expected to remain relatively loose within the visible timeframe. Last week, SMM reported global iron ore shipments of 32.26 million tonnes, up 16% month-on-month. Meanwhile, iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports totaled 30.29 million tonnes, down slightly from the previous week but up 6% year-on-year on a cumulative basis. On the news front, some traders have recently become entangled in disputes over invoices and trade documents. Market participants expect that banks and trading houses will tighten credit lines and raise margin requirements to reduce risk exposure. As a result, some participants have been forced to sell physical cargo or hedge on the exchange, amplifying the downside movement in the short term. Therefore, iron ore prices are likely to show a weak trend in the near term.

Today,the DCE iron ore futures showed weakness today. The most-traded DCE I2609 contract closed at 699.5 yuan/mt, down 0.43% from the previoustrading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose by 4-9 yuan/mt from the prior trading day. Traders offered actively, steel mills purchased mainly on a need-to basis, and overall spot trading was moderate. Fundamentally, iron ore demand saw a slight short-term recovery. According to SMM statistics, this week (August 1-7), the impact on hot metal from blast furnace maintenance was 1.3736 million mt, down 112,200 mt WoW. Next week (August 8-14), the impact is expected at 1.4252 million mt, up 51,600 mt WoW. Amid the narrative of recovering demand, downside support for iron ore prices strengthened. In the short term, iron ore prices are likely to move sideways.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended higher today. DCE's most-traded I2609 contract closed at 706 yuan/mt, up 0.93% from the previous trading session.Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose 3-8 yuan/mt from the prior trading day. Traders quoted actively, while steel mills purchased as needed, leaving overall spot trading moderate. The latest SMM survey data showed blast furnace operating rates at steel mills at 89.04%, up 0.11 percentage points MoM. Blast furnace capacity utilization rate was 88.80%, down 0.1 percentage points MoM. Daily average hot metal production at sampled mills stood at 2.4058 million mt, down 2,900 mt MoM. Due to increased maintenance at steel mills, pig iron production next week is expected to edge down, but given the short maintenance cycles, short-term iron ore demand remains fairly stable. On the news front, as the false invoice incidents continue to unfold, credit institutions are expected to tighten risk exposure, potentially hampering liquidity in short-term iron ore trade. On balance, short-term iron ore prices are likely to move sideways.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures moved steadily today. The most-traded DCE I2609 contract closed at 716.5 yuan/mt, up 0.35% from the previous session.Spot prices at Qingdao Port averaged a decline of about 0-2 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Trader activity was moderate, steel mills purchased as needed, and overall spot transactions were modest. This week, iron ore exhibited a supply-demand weakness trend. SMM's latest statistics show that iron ore inventory at 35 major ports nationwide totaled 146.39 million mt, down 420,000 mt WoW. Meanwhile, the daily average port pick-up volume edged down 45,000 mt to 3.095 million mt. The supply side, affected by earlier shipping pace and weather factors, saw port arrivals edge down. On the demand side, some blast furnaces underwent maintenance this week, and SMM's daily average pig iron production dropped to 2.4058 million mt, dragging iron ore demand lower. In terms of fundamentals, shortterm iron ore prices may lean toward consolidation.

Today, the iron ore market showed a slightly weaker trend on the futures side. The DCE main contract I2609 closed at 713.5 yuan/ton, down 0.35%from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port declined by an average of about 0-2 yuan/ton from the previous day. Trading activity among merchants was subdued, while steel mills remained cautious and preferred to wait and see, resulting in relatively limited spot transaction volumes so far this week. Iron ore supply remained largely stable this week. According to SMM statistics, global iron ore shipments totaled 32.24 million tonnes last week, holding steady week-on-week; iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports reached 29.68 million tonnes, down slightly by 2% month-on-month. On the news front, the strike at Port Hedland continues to progress, with approximately 150 workers having joined the action so far. However, the strike's short-term impact on iron ore supply has been limited, and the market reaction has been relatively muted. text:
Today, the iron ore market showed a relatively strong performance on the futures market. The DCE main contract I2609 closed at 721.5 yuan/ton,up 1.26% from the previous trading session. Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose by an average of about 3-6 yuan/ton from the previous trading day. Traders were generally active in quoting prices in line with market conditions, while steel mills purchased according to their needs, with overall spot trading volume remaining moderate so far. In the short term, changes in the fundamental supply-demand balance of iron ore itself are relatively small, though there is an expectatition of a modest uptick in demand. According to SMM statistics, the hot metal impact volume from blast furnace maintenance this week is 1.4057 million tons, down 34,400 tons from last week's maintenance impact. Next week, the hot metal impact volume is expected to be 1.3498 million tons, down 55,900 tons from this week. At the same time, coke and coking coal futures performed strongly today, with market sentiment turning optimistic toward the ferrous metals complex, which in turn boosted iron.

Today, the iron ore futures moved steadily today. The most-traded DCE I2609 contract closed at 720.5 yuan/mt, up 0.14% from the previous session.Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell by 0-2 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Traders mostly priced based on market conditions, while steel mills mainly procured on a rigid demand basis, leaving total spot volumes relatively low so far. Iron ore demand support weakened slightly this week. SMM data showed the blast furnace operating rate across 242 steel mills at 88.91%, down 0.13 percentage points WoW. The sample mills' daily average hot metal output was 2.4005 million mt, down 5,300 mt WoW. On the news front, rumors remain frequent and hard to verify. The market focused on progress in long-term contract negotiations with mines, with most funds staying on the sidelines awaiting further confirmation of direction. Overall, ore prices may continue to consolidate in the near term, but iron ore's own fundamentals currently cannot drive a trending move, leaving the overall market still dependent on news-driven catalysts.

Iron ore futures edged lower today. The DCE front-month contract I2609 seƩled at RMB 705/tonne, down 0.21% from the previous trading session.Spot prices at Qingdao Port were broadly unchanged from the prior trading day. Traders largely followed the market, with mills purchasing on an as-needed basis; overall spot transaction volumes remain modest as of this point. SMM's latest ten-port inventory survey shows total portside stocks at 106.95 million tonnes, up marginally by 360,000 tonnes week-on-week. Within the breakdown, fine concentrate and lump ore continued to draw down, while fines and pellets recorded a slight build. Fine concentrate prices remain firm, having rebounded after the pullback seen in recent weeks. Fines prices, by contrast, have held steady, weighed by elevated inventory levels and relatively stable - albeit subdued - demand. On the macro sentiment front, most market participants are currently cautious given lingering uncertainty over downstream newsflow, and are inclined to adopt a waitand-see stance. In the near term, iron ore prices are expected to trade within a narrow range from a fundamentals perspective, with limited upside and downside alike.

text:
Iron ore futures traded firmer today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 710.5/mt, up 0.42% from the previous session. Spot prices atQingdao Port rose RMB 5-9/mt from the previous trading day. Traders were active in offering, while mills showed limited enquiry, leaving overall spot transaction volumes moderate as of press time. According to the latest SMM statistics, total iron ore inventories across China's 35 major ports stood at 146.78 million mt, up 390,000 mt week-on-week - a modest build. Average daily port outbound volumes edged down 7,000 mt to 3.088 million mt. The data show that while both arrivals and port outflows declined during the period, the expected increase in arrivals outpaces the extent of any recovery in outbound shipments. Meanwhile, pig iron output remains unsteady amid fluctuating blast furnace maintenance, and under a pattern of strong supply against weak demand, iron ore inventories are likely to tilt towards accumulation. Accordingly, with the news flow in a vacuum and capital largely on the sidelines, iron ore prices are likely to trend weaker.

Iron ore futures firmed modestly today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 714/mt, up 0.85% from the previous session.Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose RMB 2-3/mt from the previous trading day. Traders were reasonably active in offering, while mill purchases were largely restocking on a just-in-need basis, leaving overall spot transaction volumes moderate.Iron ore fundamentals remained steady this week, with demand likely to contract slightly in the near term. According to SMM statistics, hot metal output affected by blast furnace maintenance came in at 1.3317 million mt this week, an increase of 20,600 mt from the previous week. Next week, the volume of hot metal affected by blast furnace maintenance is expected to reach 1.3682 million mt, up 36,500 mt from this week. On the news front, the two sides in the Port Hedland strike have yet to reach agreement on pay. The strike has now run for a month; although the impact on overall shipments has been limited, the unfolding situation has lent some bullish support to market sentiment. On balance, iron ore prices may lean bullish in the near term under the guidance of sentiment, though the bearish pattern over the medium to long term remains unchanged.

text:
Iron ore futures traded firmer today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 712/mt, up 0.78% from the previous trading day.Spot prices at Qingdao Port declined by RMB 2-3/mt. Traders were reasonably active in offering, but mill purchases remained largely restocking on a just-in-need basis, leaving overall spot transactions fairly subdued. According to SMM research data, the blast furnace capacity utilisation rate across the 242 sample steel mills stood at 88.84% this period, up 0.24 percentage points week-on-week. Average daily pig iron output came in at 2.4069 million mt, up 6,400 mt week-on-week - a modest rebound after two consecutive weeks of decline, lending phased support to iron ore prices on the demand side. In terms of market structure, demand for medium- and low-grade ore is already showing signs of picking up. That said, against a backdrop of rising coking coal and coke prices, mills' raw material procurement costs have moved higher and their acceptance of high-priced iron ore remains limited. On balance, iron ore prices are expected to maintain a rangebound pattern in the near term.

Iron ore futures traded weak today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 707/mt, down 1.19% from the previous trading day.Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell RMB 4-5/mt. Traders showed low enthusiasm in offering, while mills restocked on an as-needed basis at a measured pace, leaving overall spot transactions light. SMM's latest inventory data for the 10 key ports show total stocks at 105.40 million mt, down 1.55 million mt week-on-week. Apart from a slight build in concentrate, lump ore, pellets and fines all posted drawdowns. In the near term, iron ore demand remains stable. On fundamentals, iron ore prices are likely to trade rangebound in the near term, with any directional move depending more on how news flow transmits through the market.

IRON ORE INDEX SPECIFICATIONS, COMPILATION RATIONALE AND DATA EXCLUSIONS
Iron Ore Index Compilation Rationale and Data Exclusions
MMi iron ore indices are compiled from data provided by companies that
are part of the iron ore supply chain and involved in spot market transac-
tions. The indices are calculated using detailed transaction-level data
submitted to MMi by these companies. This data is normalised to the
appropriate specifications and screened to remove outliers before
volume-weighted average prices are calculated from the remaining core
set of data.
* Number of price submissions for iron ore indices that were excluded from
index calculations today as they were anomalous and could not be verified
IRON ORE DOMESTIC CONCENTRATE INDEX CALCULATION METHODOLOGY
The compilation method for price index generally refers to the compilation method of CPI price index and other price indices, breakdown the price data and calculate the average value according
to a certain method, taking the vertical axis as the regional composite index (average of different grade index) and the horizontal axis as the grade composite index (average of different regional
index), a total composite index for domestic ore can be output ultimately. The process system is also adopted in the calculation i.e. each sub-index can be obtained as well.

Iron ore futures traded steady today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 707.5/mt, up 0.21% from the previous trading day.Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose by RMB 1-4/mt. Traders largely followed the market, while mills purchased on an as-needed basis, leaving overall spot transaction volumes moderate. Both supply and demand for iron ore saw notable shiŌs this week. The latest statistics show total iron ore inventories across China's 35 major ports at 145.54 million mt, down 1.24 million mt week-on-week - a modest decline overall. Average daily port outbound volumes rose 48,000 mt week-on-week to 3.136 million mt. A typhoon is expected to make landfall next week, which may disrupt iron ore arrivals, and this phased contraction on the supply side should lend support to iron ore prices. In addition, expectations of a coke price hike are building, while gains in steel prices have stalled and mill margins are broadly under pressure - factors that may cap the upside for iron ore prices. On balance, absent further impetus from the news flow, iron ore prices are expected to hold a rangebound pattern in the near term.

text:
Today, the DCE iron ore futures consolidated and rose today. The most-traded contract, I2701, closed at 716 yuan/mt, up 1.27% from the previoustrading day. Spot prices at Qingdao port rose by 6-10 yuan/mt, with traders actively selling while steel mills adopted a wait-and-see sentiment, resulting in limited overall spot trading volume. According to SMM shipping data, global iron ore shipments totaled 33.17 million mt last week, edging down 1% MoM, with a cumulative YoY growth of 1%. Meanwhile, as the impact of the typhoon faded, port unloading efficiency improved. Last week, China's iron ore arrivals totaled 30.78 million mt, rebounding sharply by 65% WoW, with a cumulative YoY increase of 4.6%. This week, supply pressure has increased significantly, posing some pressure on ore prices. However, driven by expectations of demand during the traditional "September-October peak season", market sentiment turned positive, coupled with rising expectations of macro-level fiscal and financial policies to boost domestic demand. Iron ore futures prices followed the strength in steel products. However, considering that iron ore's own fundamentals remain weak, and rising coke prices further squeeze steel mill profits, ore prices face significant upward resistance. Although prices may hold up well in the short term, the upside is expected to be limited.

text:
Today, the DCE iron ore futures consolidated on a subdued note. The most-traded I2701 contract on DCE closed at 713.5 yuan/mt, down 0.28%from the previous trading day. Spot prices at Qingdao port fell by 0-2 yuan/mt, traders sold at market prices, and steel mills restocked as needed. The overall spot trading sentiment was sluggish, with trading volume slightly up from yesterday. According to SMM statistics, this week (August 22 to August 28), blast furnace maintenance affected a total of 1.4337 million mt of hot metal production, an increase of 67,400 mt WoW. Looking ahead to next week (August 29 to September 4), the hot metal production impact is expected to pull back to 1.2633 million mt, down 170,400 mt WoW. Affected by the rise in coke prices squeezing steel mill profits and the still uncertain recovery of traditional peak-season demand, some steel mills chose to postpone their production resumptions. It is expected that this week's hot metal production will edge down, steel mills' raw material purchasing sentiment will become cautious, thereby puƫng pressure on futures and spot prices, and the iron ore market may maintain a fluctuating trend in the short term.

Today, the DCE iron ore futures consolidated on a strong note. The most-traded I2701 futures contract on DCE closed at 720 yuan/mt,up 0.49% from the previous trading day. Spot prices of mainstream varieties rose by 2-7 yuan/mt, with traders adjusting to market conditions and maintaining a stable pace of shipments. Steel mills adopted a cautious wait-and-see aƫtude, and their purchasing enthusiasm pulled back. Overall spot market transaction sentiment was sluggish, with trading volume lower than yesterday. According to a SMM survey, on August 26, the blast furnace operating rate of 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 89.13%, down 0.06 ppt MoM. The blast furnace capacity utilization rate stood at 88.41%, down 0.43 ppt MoM. Daily average hot metal production at sample steel mills was 2.3953 million mt, down 11,600 mt MoM. Hot metal output has hit a boƩom, and a slight uptick may be seen next week. Market expectations have improved, providing some support for ore prices. Going forward, close attention should be paid to the squeezing effect of consecutive coke price hikes on steel mill profits, and whether hot metal output can achieve growth as expected. These will be key factors influencing ore price trends.

text:
Iron ore futures consolidated on a strong note today. The most-traded DCE I2701 contract closed at 726.5 yuan/mt, up 0.14% fromthe previous trading day. Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose by 1-2 yuan/mt overall, with steel mills mostly purchasing as needed. Traders showed moderate quoting enthusiasm, largely following market trends. Overall spot trading activity was moderate. From a fundamental perspective, supply side, port arrivals of iron ore fell by about 26% WoW recently due to typhoon disruptions, providing some short-term support for ore prices. Demand side, SMM survey results show that the daily average hot metal production in September is expected to edge up by 23,000 mt MoM. However, given that coke prices have been rising and squeezing steel mill profits, some blast furnaces originally scheduled to resume production may extend maintenance. Overall, iron ore demand growth is expected to remain mild, with peakseason demand characteristics not yet evident. As such, iron ore prices are likely to consolidate on a strong note in the short term.

Iron ore futures traded softer today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 714.0/mt, down 1.11% from theprevious trading day.Spot prices at Qingdao Port fell in step by around RMB 10-13/mt. The pullback in futures dragged spot offers lower, while mills showed stronger willingness to restock on dips, lifting overall trading activity slightly. SMM research data this week show the blast furnace capacity utilisation rate at 88.88%, up 0.47 percentage points week-on-week, while average daily hot metal output at sample steel mills came in at 2.4080 million mt, up 12,700 mt week-on-week. Driven by a modest recovery in overseas steel demand, iron ore demand has warmed at the margin, providing firm support to the floor for ore prices. Although the coke market continues to dominate sentiment in the near term, there are as yet no signs of mills cuƫng production due to tight coke supply. On balance, iron ore prices are likely to extend a pattern of a rising floor and a rangebound-to-firmer trend in the near term.

text:
Iron ore futures traded firmer on Wednesday. The DCE most-traded I2701 contract settled at 726.5 yuan/mt, up 1.32% fromthe previous session. Qingdao port spot prices rose by an average of 12-14 yuan/mt, with traders showing only moderate enthusiasm in offering and mills buying on an as-needed basis. Overall spot trading activity was lacklustre. Current market structure points to signs of a structural inflection in iron ore demand, with mills favouring cost-effective fines over higher-premium pellet and lump. SMM survey data on major port inventories showed fines destocking for a second consecutive week, while destocking in concentrate and lump slowed and pellet stocks edged higher. Total sample inventories stood at 104.82 million mt, down 20,000 mt week-on-week. Meanwhile, with coke prices continuing to climb, mills in some regions have begun considering output cuts on tight coke supply and adjusting production schedules accordingly, which could weigh on near-term iron ore demand. Overall, gains in iron ore prices are likely to slow, with the market shifting into a range-bound pattern in the near term.

Iron ore futures traded firmer today. The DCE most-active contract I2701 settled at RMB 734.5/mt, up 1.17% fromthe previous trading day. Spot prices at Qingdao Port rose by an average of RMB 1-9/mt. Traders were only moderately active in offering, while mills were largely on the sidelines, leaving overall spot trading activity subdued. On fundamentals, iron ore supply edged higher. According to SMM observations, global iron ore shipments totalled 34.45 million mt as of the end of last week, up 14% week-on-week and broadly flat year-on-year on a cumulative basis. Shipments from Australia, Brazil and other non-mainstream countries all posted modest gains, with the exception of South Africa. Over the same period, China's total iron ore arrivals came in at 26.91 million mt, up 19% week-on-week and up 4.2% year-on-year on a cumulative basis. Elsewhere, SMM understands that trading in iron ore call options has been fairly active in overseas markets, reflecting continued confidence among funds in the outlook. On balance, iron ore prices in the near term are likely to be driven more by capital flows and to extend a firmer trend on sentiment, though developments in the negotiations still warrant attention.

text:
Iron ore futures traded firmer on Tuesday. The DCE most-traded I2701 contract settled at 744.5 yuan/mt, up 1.36% fromthe previous session. Qingdao port spot prices rose by an average of 6-7 yuan/mt, with traders showing only moderate enthusiasm in offering and mills largely holding to the sidelines. Overall spot trading activity was subdued. Sustained gains in raw material prices have lifted production costs at steel mills and kept margins under pressure, prompting those with heavier losses to step up maintenance and trimming rigid demand for iron ore. SMM survey data showed hot metal output lost to blast furnace maintenance came to 1.3834 million mt this week, up 23,600 mt from the previous week. On the supply side, however, tight vessel availability and higher diesel costs have kept international dry bulk freight rates climbing, lending cost support to iron ore prices. Coupled with strong market expectations for the traditional peak season in September and October, funds have pushed futures higher. Iron ore prices may therefore decouple from fundamentals for a time, holding a firm tone on sentiment in the near term.

Iron ore futures opened weaker on Wednesday before recovering through the session. The DCE most-traded I2701 contractsettled at 738.5 yuan/mt, down 0.27% from the previous session. Qingdao port spot prices fell by an average of around 8 yuan/mt, with traders showing only moderate enthusiasm in offering and mills reluctant to buy. Overall spot trading was subdued. SMM survey data on steel mills showed the blast furnace operating rate at 89.08%, down 0.48 percentage point week-on-week, while average daily pig iron output slipped by 5,200 mt to 2.4028 million mt. Mills that have been running at a loss are progressively entering maintenance, weighing on iron ore prices from the fundamentals side. On the news front, progress in long-term contract negotiations has fuelled expectations of lower import prices ahead. That sentiment has fed through to the spot market, leaving mills broadly reluctant to buy at prevailing levels and pushing procurement demand lower, which continues to pressure prices. Iron ore prices look set to shift into a softer, range-bound pattern in the near term.

Iron ore futures were weaker today. The DCE most-traded I2701 contract settled at 718 yuan/mt, down 1.78% from the previous session.Qingdao port spot prices fell 8-13 yuan/mt on average. Traders were reasonably active and mills bought largely to cover immediate needs. Spot trading was thin. With the latest round of coke price increases now in effect, mill profitability has narrowed further. The market is concerned mills may begin cuƫng output, which would weigh on iron ore demand. On fundamentals, supply remains comfortable. SMM data showed stocks across 35 major Chinese ports at 143.49 million mt, down 420,000 mt week on week, a smaller draw than in recent weeks. Average daily port outbound volume rose 90,000 mt to 3.235 million mt. On demand, most mills are running at a loss but only a handful have production cut plans, so the actual impact on demand is limited. On the macro side, tensions in the Middle East continue to build. Houthi forces in Yemen have tightened control around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, lifting oil prices and trade risk. Expectations of further Federal Reserve rate rises have also strengthened. Together these have reinforced a bearish market outlook and commodities are broadly under pressure. Iron ore prices are likely to stay weak in the near term, driven by news flow and sentiment.

Futures and spot have split: spot declines are slowing and Carajas fines held flat for a second day, yet the board broke below710 high coke prices are forcing maintenance, turning feared cuts into real ones
Today brought the first real divergence of this decline: spot is slowing while the board is accelerating. Declines narrowed across all five MMi indices port spot from -1.00%/-0.84%/-0.62% the previous session to -0.43%/-0.24%/-0.15% and seaborne from -0.97%/-1.29% to -0.52%/-0.92% and Carajas nes held at at 834 yuan/wmt for a second day, yet the DCE most-traded contract still fell 9.5 yuan, breaking below 710 to 708.5 yuan/mt. Futures falling harder than spot means the board is pricing the demand gap ahead, not today's trading. That gap became concrete today. SMM's evening review notes that with coking coal and coke prices staying high, some mills have already entered maintenance on tight coke supply, weakening essential iron ore demand. Notably, SMM's own cost table that morning still said only isolated mills had cut plans with limited real impact the read moved from "feared but not happening" to "partly in maintenance" within a single day. And the trigger is tight coke supply rather than losses alone, which means the pace of cuts will be set by coke availability and need not ease as ore prices fall. The next hot metal and operating rate prints are the key test. Supply shows no sign of relenting: global shipments reached 37.4058 million mt last week, a second consecutive increase with Australia above 20 million mt for the first time, while arrivals merely held steady the extra tonnage is still stacked in transit. SMM sums up the port picture as high stocks, slow draws and slow builds, with the 35-port drawdown already markedly slower. On the cost side import losses widened to -9.15 yuan/mt, and domestic ore's relative strength is loosening too, with Shandong 64% alkaline concentrate down 4 yuan to 816. On balance prices look set to stay soft near term, though spot has begun to resist ahead of the board.

text:
After six straight sessions lower, the market has given a clear stabilisation signal. The DCE most-traded contract fell just 1.0 yuanto 707.5 yuan/mt, against 9.5 the day before; more importantly, spot split for the first time in this leg - Carajas fines rose 4 yuan to 838 and PB lump 3 yuan to 870 yuan/wmt while mid and low grades slipped another 2. High grade turning up is not an isolated move: C3 Brazil→China freight climbed in step to USD 42.02/mt, another period high, and rising long-haul costs support high-grade prices directly. What really deserves a rethink is demand. For two days running SMM's cost table has stressed that some mills have entered maintenance on tight coke supply and that essential iron ore demand is weakening - yet SMM's own weekly maintenance survey points the other way: hot metal lost to blast furnace maintenance is 1.4157 million mt this week, down 57,600 mt WoW, and is projected 42,300 mt lower again next week at 1.3734 million mt, with long-product maintenance losses falling in step. Maintenance pressure is easing, not building - and that is the fundamental basis for prices stopping where they did. The longer-run contraction is nonetheless real: NBS puts August pig iron output at 67.65 million mt, -3.5% YoY, with Jan-Aug down 3.1%. Costs have not eased either, with the average imported ore margin falling from -9.15 to -10.61 yuan/mt, leaving sellers very little room to concede. On balance, prices look set to shift from a one-way decline into low-level consolidation, and the high-grade premium has already begun to recover - the 65% port spot index held flat, the 58% slipped just 1 yuan and the 61% fell 5, widening the high-low spread from 183 to 184 yuan/wmt. Two things to verify: whether the next 242-mill hot metal print rises as maintenance losses fall, and when last week's shipment surge (+8.59%) finally lands in port stocks - that remains the supply pressure hanging overhead.

Both of today's developments point the same way: yesterday's encouraging signals were not solid. First, futures and spot swapped roles- the DCE most-traded contract rose 1.5 yuan to 709.0 yuan/mt, its first gain after six sessions lower, while spot fell another 2 yuan across the board and Carajas fines and PB lump, which led yesterday's turn, gave back 2 yuan each. High grade's solo run lasted a single session. The direct cause sits on the cost side: C5 Australia→China freight fell 3.66% in a day to USD 17.12/mt and C3 Brazil→China ended its run of gains, easing to 41.79 - the long-haul cost factor that had supported high grade is gone. Second, and more importantly: the previous issue argued from two weeks of falling maintenance losses that hot metal should recover, and today's data refuted it. SMM's survey puts daily average hot metal across 242 mills at 2.3991 million mt, down a further 3,700 mt, with the operating rate at 88.93%. SMM attributes this to the lagged effect of earlier maintenance - losses are falling, but output lost to earlier work is still feeding through. The decline did narrow (-5,200 to -3,700 mt) and one furnace is due to restart next week, though SMM warns that deepening mill losses could bring unplanned maintenance and leave output short of that. Note that CISA's series points the other way, with early-September pig iron at key enterprises up 1.7% per day; the samples and periods differ, and this report uses SMM's 242-mill basis throughout. Supply has a new variable: the union's negotiating proposal at Port Hedland was formally rejected. No strike has been reported, but this is Australia's largest iron ore export terminal and Australian shipments have just hit a record 20.7583 million mt, so industrial action would bite. On balance, prices should keep trading in a range with a soft centre - SMM's current view too. A genuine turn requires hot metal itself to rise, not merely maintenance losses to fall.

text: There is one central fact this period: pre-holiday restocking has genuinely arrived, and at scale. Imported ore stocks at 242 millsrose 4.37 million mt in a week to 78.61 million (+5.89%), with days of consumption rebuilt from 19.3 to 20.5 - ending the two-week pattern of mills running lean and refusing to restock. Prices responded: Qingdao Port spot rose 5-11 yuan/wmt and the DCE contract gained 5.0 yuan to 715.5 yuan/mt, up for a third straight session. Two qualifications matter. First, SMM states plainly that "with restocking nearing its end, price support is weakening", and reports mills buying only essential volumes with spot trading thin - this is passive pre-holiday cover, not a demand expansion. Second, and more important: ports have turned back to building. The 35 ports ended their run of draws and rose 840,000 mt to 144.33 million, with outflows down to 3.21 million mt. SMM's outlook for next week is blunter still: the lagged effect of earlier shipments will lift arrivals while demand fails to improve and outflows stay weak, so port stocks should build again with the pressure increasing. In other words, mills built this cover precisely as ports began to accumulate. Two further threads are worth noting. SMM's analysis concludes this decline was driven from outside China - the SGX contract fell 2.43% on the week, twice the DCE's 1.05%, while Chinese futures and spot fell almost identically, leaving the domestic pricing chain running smoothly; and the Fed's first rate hike in three years landed, within expectations but still a drag on upside. Today's indices reinforce it: all four domestic readings rose (the 65% port spot index +0.60% to 843, the 61% +0.58% to 689) while the 65% seaborne index fell 0.48% to USD 113.40/dmt; the high-low spread widened another 4 yuan to 196 yuan/wmt, a fifth straight session and 13 yuan up from 183 on Sep 14. On balance prices should keep trading in a narrow range with a soft centre, in line with SMM's view.

What the previous issue flagged has happened: arrivals at Chinese ports jumped 4.41 million mt to 31.32 million last week(+16.39%), +4.8% YTD. This is the lagged delivery of the two weeks of heavy shipments that peaked at 37.4058 million mt, when Australia first cleared 20 million. Global shipments have themselves fallen back 8.02% to 34.4065 million mt with both Australia and Brazil easing - the shipment peak has passed, but the arrival peak has only just begun. Today the market showed a textbook case of both sides strengthening at once: arrivals surging on supply, pre-holiday restocking still running on demand. The two offset each other and prices stayed in a narrow band - the DCE contract slipped 0.5 yuan to 715.0 yuan/mt, spot was 2 yuan above Friday and flat against Sunday, and the port spot indices gave back 1-2 yuan. The durability of those two forces is very different, however. SMM has said plainly that restocking is nearing its end and mills are increasingly inclined to buy only on dips, and mill imported ore stocks were already rebuilt to 78.61 million mt with 20.5 days of cover last week, so there is limited room left. The arrivals, by contrast, will only show up in the next port inventory print - and the 35 ports had already turned to a build a week earlier. The cost side offers one positive: the average imported ore margin turned from -2.84 to +6.48 yuan/mt, the first profit of this decline, with C5 freight ending its slide and rebounding 1.87%. But domestic ore is loosening in step - mine capacity utilisation is back to 58.2%, concentrate output up 28,000 mt, and Hebei concentrate already down 10-20 yuan/mt. On balance prices should stay rangebound with a soft centre. What matters is the gap in timing between restocking ending and arrivals landing: once the buying stops while port stocks accelerate, the lower bound of the range will be tested again.

text:
Today brought two bearish threads and one clear floor beneath them. The first is fundamental: maintenance losses have been revised up again- on SMM's latest review basis, hot metal lost to blast furnace maintenance is 1.5267 million mt this week (Sep 19 25), up 56,000 mt WoW, rising a further 46,600 mt to 1.5733 million next week (Sep 26-Oct 2), each figure 24,500 mt above the Sep 21 weekly summary. Set against the Sep 14 print (1.4157 million this week, falling to 1.3734 million next), the direction has completely reversed: sustained mill losses are translating into steadily wider output cuts, and SMM says explicitly that the support this gives ore prices is weakening. The second is news flow: talk of low-grade ore being released circulated again today, souring sentiment and dragging prices lower. If confirmed it would add directly to tradeable port supply, compounding last week's 4.41 million mt surge in arrivals. The floor comes from the one part of demand that has not weakened - pre-holiday restocking is not yet complete. On that basis SMM sees strong downward resistance and expects the decline to be limited, and spot bears it out: traders held quotes relatively firm, spot fell 3-5 yuan against the board's 1%, and Carajas fines gave up just 4 yuan. Costs have not deteriorated either - SMM's cost table this period calls import margins broadly stable, expecting them only to edge lower, rather than the clear squeeze that falling spot and rising freight would imply. Note that this report's reading from maintenance data and the arrival surge leans toward the lower bound being tested further, while SMM lands on a limited decline. These are not in conflict so much as on different time horizons: the restocking floor is short-lived and already depleting (mill stocks were rebuilt to 78.61 million mt with 20.5 days of cover last week), whereas wider maintenance and landing arrivals are persistent. What matters, then, is the timing gap: whether restocking ends before port stocks start building. The next port inventory print is the week's most important observation, and the low-grade release rumour is the second variable to watch closely.

text: The story today is not the board's 4-yuan bounce but the first structural flip in spot. The past week ran on Carajas fines holdingbest and the high-low spread widening six sessions in a row; today it turned completely: PB fines, Newman fines, BRBF and PB lump each rose 3 yuan, SSF rose 3 yuan for a market-leading +0.56%, while Carajas fines fell 2 yuan to 842 and Newman lump 2 yuan. The flip has a clear industrial logic: with losses deepening and production appetite weakening, lowering the charged grade and substituting mid and low grades for high grade is the most direct cost compression available, and today's price distribution is its signature. Note this runs opposite to the earlier "low-grade release" rumour - a supply-side release would weigh on low grade, yet low grade led the gains, so the driver is demand-side grade switching. Aggregate demand, meanwhile, keeps deteriorating. SMM's survey puts hot metal at 2.3943 million mt, down for a third straight week, with the decline widening from last week's 3,700 mt to 4,800 mt; four furnaces entered maintenance against three restarts. More important is SMM's forward view: more mills are scheduling maintenance, and hot metal may fall more sharply once October begins, strengthening expectations of supply-side contraction. Set against maintenance losses of 1.5267 million mt this week and 1.5733 million next, the pressure is extending into October. Costs have not improved either - SMM calls import margins lower and expects them to stay choppy. SMM does not credit fundamentals for the bounce either - "fundamentals remain bearish, but the board firmed slightly on market talk of reduced Brazilian shipments" - a second straight rumour-driven session after yesterday's bearish low-grade release, with SMM expecting prices under pressure as restocking ends and arrivals rise. text: What several issues have been flagging has now landed: ports have formally turned to building. The 10-port total rose to 102.594 million mt,+681,500 mt WoW, ending three straight weeks of draws, with the 35-port series up in step to 145.45 million mt (+1.12 million mt). The product mix is unambiguous - the entire build is fines (+808,100 mt) while concentrates, lump and pellets all drew down. That is exactly how last week's 4.41 million mt surge in arrivals (+16.39%) shows up: the increment is fines, and it lands at the ports. The build is only half the picture, though. Outflows rose the same day, up 25,000 mt to 3.235 million mt, and SMM's wording is "arrivals up markedly, outflows lifted somewhat by pre-holiday restocking, yet ports still building modestly" - restocking is still holding the floor, just no longer holding it up. SMM's view for next week is blunt: arrivals keep rising, mill stocks keep accumulating, restocking support weakens. On price structure, today calls for a correction of my own. Yesterday Carajas fines fell 2 yuan while SSF rose 3, and the previous issue read that as mills shifting their burden mix down amid deepening losses. Today reversed completely - Carajas fines jumped 9 yuan to 851 while SSF slipped 1. That reading lasted a single session, so the last two days look more like short-term noise than a structural switch; today's strength in Carajas fines fits better with C3 Brazil→China freight rising to USD 43.38/mt (+0.84%). The onshore/offshore split persists: the DCE rose for a second session to 713.5 yuan/mt while SGX fell through 96 to USD 96.04/dmt, and domestic ore weakened in step, the composite index down to 831.59 yuan/mt (-0.70%). The indices sent a different signal today than yesterday: the 65% port spot index rose 2 yuan and the 65% seaborne USD 0.20, widening the high-low spread to 201 yuan/wmt, in line with the jump in Carajas fines. Where the two bases diverged yesterday, they confirm each other today, with high grade strongest on both sides.

text:
The previous issue closed by saying the build had started, restocking was on its way out, and the two lines would crossaround the National Day break - that crossing has arrived. SMM states today that "restocking demand for iron ore is largely complete and price support is weakening", and prices duly fell across the board: the DCE most-traded contract dropped 8.5 yuan to 705.0 yuan/mt and Qingdao Port spot fell 10-12 yuan/wmt, with traders quoting listlessly, mills buying only as needed and trading thin. Structurally, the "high grade alone is strong" theme of last week broke down in a single session: the MMi 61% port spot index fell 12 yuan (-1.74%), the largest of the five, against -9 for the 65% and just -2 for the 58%, so the high-low spread collapsed from 201 to 194 yuan/wmt, unwinding the entire widening of the previous four sessions. That confirms the earlier call: the past fortnight's grade divergence was noise, not trend. Supply produced a divergence worth tracking: global shipments recovered 3.21%, with Australia back above 20 million mt at 20.7633 million while Brazil fell a further 8.61% to 6.7772 million. SMM attributes Brazil's decline to high freight curbing shipments from some smaller miners - one of the few supports left, and the industrial footnote to C3's elevated level. Arrivals, meanwhile, fell 5.93%, easing pressure for now. On demand, the line that matters most is "some mills have moved maintenance plans to after the holiday because of tight coke supply": the gap is delayed, not removed, and October's fall in hot metal may be more concentrated. CISA's mid-September pig iron output of 1.770 million mt/day (-1.4%) now aligns with SMM's sample, closing the earlier caliber gap. On balance, the restocking support has left the stage and prices lack support, staying soft near term - in line with SMM's conclusion. Three things to watch after the holiday: the actual size of October's hot metal decline, whether Brazilian shipments recover as freight eases, and the slope of the port build.
